newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state to sell off preserved food firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state to sell off preserved food firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state-owned Holding Company for Food Industries said on Friday it was offering 90 percent of its Edfina Preserved Foods for sale to one or more anchor investors through sealed bids.
The parent company said in a published advertisement the investors could either:
- Buy two plants in the Mediterranean city of Port Said and another one in the nearby city of Damietta; or
- Lease the two Port Said plants.
Bids are to be submitted in the name of the chairman of the holding company. Envelopes will be open at noon (1000 GMT) on Wednesday, April 2.
They should be accompanied by a guarantee of five million pounds ($1.5 million) for the whole firm or 500,000 pounds for each plant, in cash or accepted cheque, the parent company said.
The firm, which owns another four plants in the city of Alexandria, has a capacity of 50,000 tonnes. Its output, however, in the financial year 95/96 was 22,465 tonnes.
The head of the technical sectors, Abdel Sattar Soleiman, can reply any queries at 202 349 2312 or fax 202 360 4026.
